purpose: Pages that delivered no content (a JavaScript wall in any wording, site navigation or footer text, lone glyphs) are recognized as title-only by the shape they share rather than by one literal string each, and a Reddit link post gets its article even when the poster wrote a note, so analysis runs on real content or is honestly labeled title-only.
form:
Two general shape rules in the one check, and two fetchers that stop preferring junk.

1. `daemon/src/prismis_daemon/readability.py` `is_readable` (line 82) keeps its placeholder checks (RSS's no-content fallback, Reddit link-only content, YouTube's no-transcript content) and the constants and `format_*` helpers the fetchers import. It replaces three narrow checks with two general ones. (a) The has-prose rule replaces the markup-only check and the anchor-only check: content is readable only if some line, after tags and URLs are removed, holds at least four words, with each CJK character (kana and CJK ideographs) counting as one word. The HN `Comments` anchor stub (one word once its tag is stripped), tag-only text, '‹ ›' and navigation lists all fail it. (b) The JavaScript-wall rule replaces the `_JS_WALL_TEXT` literal: content is a wall when a line names JavaScript with a requirement verb (enable, enabled, disable, disabled, need, needs, require, requires, required, turn on) and its visible text is under 1,200 characters. The constant carries a one-line comment naming its measurement (cerebro, 2026-10-03: walls up to 1,068 chars, real articles from 1,409). Both rules are pure functions over the content string, with no length floor on text that lacks a JavaScript notice.

2. `daemon/src/prismis_daemon/fetchers/rss.py` `_extract_full_content` (line 249) returns the extraction only when `is_readable` accepts it, and otherwise returns `_fallback_content(entry)` as it already does when extraction returns nothing.

3. `daemon/src/prismis_daemon/fetchers/reddit.py` `_to_content_item` (line 440): for a link post whose URL is neither an image nor a reddit page, and not already stored readably, it calls `extract_article` whether or not the post has self-text, and builds `format_reddit_link_only(url)`, then the self-text if any, then the article text when `is_readable` accepts it. Text posts, image, video and reddit-internal links, and the already-readable skip behave as today. `refetch_one` gets this through `_to_content_item` unchanged.

4. `docs/architecture/boundaries.md` line 56 becomes: no length floor on its own; readability is judged by content shape, and a size bound may only qualify a failure-shape signal (the JavaScript-wall rule), never stand alone.

5. Tests in `daemon/tests/unit/test_readability_unit.py`: not readable for the stoppels.ch extraction, '‹ ›', the YouTube footer list, the Mastodon and Notion notices, nature.com's notice, and the existing failure fixtures; readable for the existing one-sentence blurb and two-line question, a Japanese news paragraph with no spaces, a 1,500-char article containing 'Loading... (JavaScript required)', a README line '- No JavaScript required' inside a long document, and content that merely contains a link. Fetcher tests serve pages from a local HTTP server (no live third-party URL): RSS falls back to the entry summary when the page extracts to navigation text and keeps a readable extraction; a Reddit link post with self-text gets the article appended, and a failed or unreadable extraction leaves link plus self-text. Each new test is shown red with its rule removed.
commitments: One check, `is_readable` in readability.py, still decides readability for every consumer; no second check is added.
Text with no line of at least four words (tags and URLs removed, CJK characters counted one each) is not readable.
A JavaScript-requirement line makes content a wall only when its visible text is under 1,200 characters; text without such a line is never judged by its size.
A fetcher never prefers an extraction the check rejects over its own fallback.
A Reddit link post to an external article gets the article text whether or not the poster wrote self-text.
boundaries.md line 56 states the no-length-floor rule with its one permitted qualifier.
sacrifices: Reddit self-posts with no line of four words ('Pls help', 'Tada') become title-only; their title carries all there is.
A JavaScript wall longer than 1,200 visible characters stays readable; none was seen in 45 days of cerebro items.
Items already stored and analysed keep their classification until `prismis-daemon refetch` is run for them, a separate costed step.
An HN link to youtube.com is still extracted as a page and becomes title-only rather than getting the video's transcript.
Reddit link posts with self-text now cost one article fetch each per new post.
risk: If the has-prose rule rejects a real short format not seen in the 45-day sample (a list of short items with no four-word line), those items become title-only and skip deep extraction until the rule is widened; if a real article under 1,200 characters carries a JavaScript-requirement line, it is labeled title-only.
